title: Sunny Makes a Wish | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka finds a dandelion clock glowing in the moonlight, takes a big soft breath, and makes the most important wish she knows — that the bush will always be this beautiful and peaceful. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The dandelion was glowing in the moonlight.

Sunny almost walked past it. It was small, tucked between two flat stones at the edge of the track. But when the moonlight caught it, it lit up like a tiny lantern.

A perfect dandelion clock. A white sphere of seeds, each one waiting for a puff of breath to set it free.

Sunny crouched down beside it. She looked at it for a moment.

She thought very carefully about what to wish for.

Not something for herself. She had everything she needed — the bush, the moonlight, the quiet nights, the kind creatures she met.

She wanted to wish for something bigger.

She wished that the bush would always be this peaceful.

She wished that the creek would always run clear.

She wished that the stars would always come out when it was dark.

And she wished that wherever little ones were, they would always have someone to watch over them while they slept.

She took a deep, soft breath.

And blew.

The seeds scattered — upward and outward and sideways — a constellation of wishes flying into the night.

Sunny watched until the last one disappeared.

The bare stem stayed, a thin silver line in the moonlight.

Sunny sat beside it for a long time, feeling quiet and full.

Then she curled up in the soft moss nearby and slept, her wishes already on their way.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, wishes. Goodnight, little one.
